game_concept: A card battler set in Eldritch Ruins – Broken Colonnade, a row of broken columns: the relic hunter must handle ghost knights while practicing lists. Core idea – Length Limit: Use len() to stop the list from growing past the limit of Broken Colonnade.
theme: Eldritch Ruins – Broken Colonnade: a row of broken columns
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
secondary_mechanics: Hint tokens that reveal one line of code
player_objective: Assignment versus equality: declare resource as int, apply resource == 12, and print each result with %d. Dataset 9 starts with [-3, 0, 12, 15]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.
controls: Edit the C program. Run tests all streams; Step shows declarations, assignments and output. readInput() is a LogiCade game-port helper declared in logicade.h. This safe practice runtime supports a documented C subset.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Length Limit' (Week 7 slot 9), mission type 'Streak Challenge', and setting 'Broken Colonnade'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.
topic: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations

source_player_objective: Chain 6 consecutive correct decisions about capacity to power up the relic hunter and open the glyph door.
source_lose_condition: lives reach 0 (each wrong decision costs a life and resets the streak).
hint: Declare before use. int resource = readInput(); creates the named game-port value; printf uses %d.
